project.name: treetracker-wallet-admin-client
project.description: The admin panel for accessing wallets and executing all known API calls for the wallet API. Wallet owners use it to display and transfer tokens and transactions, create sub wallets, and configure their appearance.

nodes.summary: API layer for wallet transfers. Provides functions to list, accept, decline and cancel token transfers against the wallet backend.

nodes.name: acceptTransfer
nodes.summary: Accepts a pending transfer by POSTing to the transfer accept endpoint with the stored auth token.

nodes.name: declineTransfer
nodes.summary: Declines a pending transfer by POSTing to the transfer decline endpoint with the stored auth token.

nodes.name: cancelTransfer
nodes.summary: Cancels an outgoing transfer by POSTing to the transfer cancel endpoint with the stored auth token.

nodes.name: build-release.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow triggered on push to any branch. Prepares channel settings, builds the client, creates a semantic release, and deploys the artifact to S3/CloudFront.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a prepare job with outputs consumed by downstream jobs to resolve deployment channel and secret names.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Resolves the deployment channel and per-environment secret names, exposing them as job outputs for downstream jobs.

nodes.name: client
nodes.summary: Installs dependencies and builds the React client project artifact.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Runs semantic-release to create a versioned GitHub release from the build.

nodes.name: deploy
nodes.summary: Deploys the built client artifact to the resolved S3 bucket and invalidates the CloudFront CDN.

nodes.name: deploy.yaml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched GitHub Actions workflow that deploys a chosen version to a selected environment (dev/test/prod) by preparing settings, building the frontend, and pushing to S3/CloudFront.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses workflow_dispatch inputs (version and environment choice) to parameterize a targeted deployment.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Resolves environment-specific settings and secret names based on the dispatch environment input.

nodes.name: frontend

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what this project is: the Greenstand Treetracker Wallet Admin Client, a React single-page app for managing wallets, tokens, transfers, and trust relationships against the wallet API. It covers the project background, use cases, and the local development setup. Read it first to build a mental map before diving into code.

tour.title: Application Entry & Bootstrap
tour.description: src/index.js is the true entry point: it mounts the root App component into the DOM and wires web-vitals reporting. App.js is the composition root that wires together the MUI theme provider, the auth provider, the app layout shell, and the client route table. Together these two files show how the whole app is assembled from the outside in.

tour.title: Routing & App Shell
tour.description: ClientRoutes.js is the central react-router route table. It maps URLs to feature pages, wraps protected pages in their context providers, and enforces authentication before rendering. Layout.js provides the visual shell (sidebar Menu, responsive drawer) and mounts the Transfers and TrustRelationships context providers around the routed content, so navigation and shared state live side by side.

tour.title: Authentication
tour.description: Building on the App wiring from Step 2, authentication is the gate for every protected route. auth-context.js declares the shared React context for login state and logout. AuthProvider.js implements it: it manages login and logout, persists the token in localStorage, and decodes the JWT. Login.js is the page users first hit, collecting wallet, password, and API key and calling the API to sign in.
tour.languageLesson: React Context lets a provider component share values (here, auth state and actions) with any descendant via a matching useContext hook, avoiding prop drilling through every layer.

tour.title: The API Client Layer
tour.description: apiClient.js is the foundation of all backend communication: a configured axios instance with auth and API-key header helpers plus a 401 interceptor that redirects to login. The three api modules build on it, one per domain: wallets.js fetches and creates wallets and lists pending transfers, transfers.js lists, accepts, declines, and cancels token transfers, and trust_relationships.js manages the request/accept/decline/delete lifecycle of trust relationships.
tour.languageLesson: Axios interceptors run on every response; here a 401 handler centralizes session-expiry logout so individual call sites never repeat that logic.

tour.title: State Management Contexts
tour.description: Between the raw API modules from Step 5 and the pages sit three context providers that own feature state. WalletsContext holds the wallet list and row-formatting helpers, TransfersContext loads, prepares, and paginates transfers while tracking pending ones, and TrustRelationshipsContext centralizes trust-relationship state, filters, pagination, and API orchestration. Pages consume these hooks rather than calling the API directly.

tour.title: Wallets Feature
tour.description: Now we reach the first user-facing feature. MyWallets.js loads wallets through the API and renders them in a paginated table with a create-wallet action. Wallet.js is the detail view: it loads a single wallet plus its pending transfers and renders the wallet header and info blocks. These pages show the standard pattern: read from a context or API, then present with shared UI components.

tour.title: Transfers & Sending Tokens
tour.description: MyTransfers.js renders the transfers table backed by TransfersContext from Step 6 and surfaces error messages. SendTokens.js is the richest page: it orchestrates wallet selection, trusted and untrusted transfer tabs, token transfers, and wallet creation. TransferFilter.js is the shared domain model that shapes list/query parameters for the transfers API.

tour.title: Trust Relationships Feature
tour.description: Trust relationships govern which wallets may transfer tokens to each other. TrustRelationship.js renders the relationships table and status messages, TrustRelationshipTable.js drives the data grid with actions, and CreateTrustRelationship.js handles requesting a new relationship. TrustRelationShipFilter.js is the query model backing the trust-relationships API from Step 5.

tour.title: Shared UI Components & Theme
tour.description: Every page above reuses a common presentation layer. theme.js is the central MUI theme defining palette, typography, and component overrides, so the app looks consistent. Table.js is the reusable sortable, paginated data grid behind the wallet, transfer, and trust tables. Message.js and Loader.js provide standard feedback and loading states used across features.
tour.languageLesson: MUI's ThemeProvider injects a single theme object into all components via context, so design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) stay defined in one place instead of hard-coded per component.

tour.title: Project Manifest & Environment Config
tour.description: package.json declares the dependency stack seen throughout the tour (React, MUI, axios, react-router), the Create React App scripts, and the ESLint/Jest configuration and Node engine requirement. The .env files supply per-environment settings (development, production, test) such as the wallet API base URL that apiClient.js from Step 5 reads at build time.

tour.title: Build, Release & Deployment
tour.description: As a capstone, see how the app ships. build-release.yaml runs on push: it prepares channel settings, builds the client, cuts a semantic release, and deploys the artifact. deploy.yaml is the manually dispatched workflow that pushes a chosen version to a selected environment (dev, test, or prod). Together they close the loop from code to running admin panel.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers (push, workflow_dispatch) to decide when to run and 'jobs'/'steps' for the build-and-deploy sequence; workflow_dispatch enables the manual, environment-parameterized deploy here.
